sites.rationale: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing introduced an 11-aa HiBiT tag plus a GSSG linker into the endogenous SELE locus in HUVECs and TERT2-HUVECs, placing the tag immediately after signal-peptide cleavage (after A21, before W22). Surface display was confirmed with membrane-impermeable exogenous LgBiT (NanoBiT complementation), proving the tag is extracellular. Ligand-induced expression in response to TNFα (EC50 = 0.057 ± 0.011 nM), IL-1α, IL-1β, LPS, VEGF165a, and histamine was fully preserved, confirming normal trafficking and inducible expression. No disulfide cysteines, N-glycosylation sequons, or known functional residues are disrupted at this junction. The GSSG linker provides conformational flexibility away from the lectin-domain ligand-binding surface. sources.claim: (B) General genome-editing strategy showing the PAM sequence adjacent to the signal sequence of E-selectin and the insertion of HiBiT and a GSSG linker immediately following the signal sequence in the HiBiT-tagged E-selectin sequence.
